edges.description: Intracellular infection of macrophages engages cell-mediated immunity: resolution of infection depends on activation of targeted T-cell populations for cytokine production and on activation of macrophages. This is the protective arm of the response.
intermediate_mechanisms: activation of targeted T-cell populations for appropriate cytokine production
edges.target: Th1-Polarized Cell-Mediated Response and Macrophage Activation

edges.description: The same infection can instead drive a Th2-polarized T-helper response, which in the murine model is associated with disease progression rather than control.
edges.target: Th2-Polarized Response and Permissive Disease Progression

nodes.description: Promastigotes differentiate into amastigotes that multiply inside host macrophages.

evidence.reference_title: Involvement of Leishmania Phosphatases in Parasite Biology and Pathogeny.
evidence.snippet: Inside vertebrate host macrophages, the parasites can differentiate into the amastigote form and multiply

nodes.description: The protective arm of the T-helper response. Activation of targeted T-cell populations with appropriate cytokine production, together with activation of macrophages, underlies resolution of leishmanial infection; in the murine model, development of a Th1 response is associated with control of infection. This node therefore restrains the intracellular amastigote-replication node rather than promoting it.
nodes.id: Th1-Polarized Cell-Mediated Response and Macrophage Activation

evidence.snippet: Resolution of leishmanial infection is dependent on the coordinated interactions between components of cell mediated immune response, specifically the activation of targeted T-cell populations for appropriate cytokine production and activation of macrophages.
In murine model, the development of Thl response is associated with control of infection

nodes.description: The permissive arm of the T-helper response. In the murine model, a Th2 response is associated with disease progression rather than control of infection. Human data are less clear-cut, so this node is curated as a model-derived mechanism, not an established human one.
nodes.id: Th2-Polarized Response and Permissive Disease Progression

evidence.snippet: Th2 response is associated with disease progression
